profile.regional_context: Per Google's own data center location page, Google established the Council Bluffs facility in 2007 with an initial $600 million investment and has invested over $20 billion in Iowa since. A $7 billion expansion was announced to grow the Council Bluffs campus and establish a new Cedar Rapids, Iowa data center. Google also cites a NextEra Energy agreement tied to restarting Iowa's Duane Arnold nuclear plant as part of its regional power strategy, and $1.3 million toward a 47-site water quality/grade stabilization project.

reading.body:
Google does not publish individual facility power capacity, square footage, or exact addresses for its Council Bluffs campus, following its stated disclosure policy of releasing only aggregate state-level investment figures. The campus has received over $20 billion in cumulative investment since 2007, with a $7 billion expansion announced recently, but the specific power draw of this location remains undisclosed and cannot be translated into racks or accelerator counts.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities, only 2 of which publish power capacity figures totaling 18 MW. This Google campus ranks third in the state by published capacity, a ranking that reflects the absence of published data rather than confirmed specifications. The state context indicates most mapped facilities, like this one, disclose no individual power figures, making statewide capacity visibility fragmentary.

Google ties regional power strategy for Council Bluffs to a NextEra Energy agreement involving restart of the Duane Arnold nuclear plant, signaling the campus is material enough to warrant nuclear-scale generation planning. Without published capacity, this campus cannot be read against compute requirements or grid constraint arguments, only against Google's investment commitment and its strategic pairing with nuclear power.
